title: Monday Move
headline: I built an agent that posted only the competitor news it could prove
description: A weekly agent that posted only the competitor news it could verify, with one move for the team to make.
label: Case study

blocks.p: My team at work needed to know what seven competitors did each week, and that news is messy. Articles get republished, and some never say when the event happened. Hand that to a model and old news comes back sounding new.

Monday Move was a Claude Code scheduled task I wrote and ran myself. At 8am every Monday it searched the past seven days and rated each finding: High if it could change deals or open a market, Medium if worth watching, Low if noise, which was logged but never posted. Each Slack post led with this week's move: one thing to do.

blocks.alt: A Slack post headed with this week's move, followed by a high-impact and a medium-impact signal, each with a date, an angle and a source link, and a footer counting 2 verified and 4 discarded.
blocks.caption: The Monday post, rebuilt with invented companies. The real ones stay private.

blocks.p: The hardest call was trading volume for trust. Eight items look busier than three, but the prompt ranked them the other way: three verified signals made a good run, and eight unverified ones a failed one. Every finding needed a source and a confirmed date for the event itself, because a republished article carries a fresh date. A failed check meant dropping the item and never replacing it with a weaker one. A quiet week said "no verified signals."

blocks.alt: A signal log with three verified rows, each with a competitor, type, date, impact and source, above a list of four checked and discarded candidates with the reason each was dropped.
blocks.caption: Verified signals went to a log. Each run also listed what it dropped, with the reason.

blocks.p: First, the agent had to write out today's date and the date seven days back, then use that start date in every query. And the notes I gave it on each competitor could never be reported as news.

It ran about 32 times. A typical move, from July: a rival had shipped, in about four weeks, a targeting feature we expected two to three quarters out, so the line said to update that rival's battlecard now.
